::: small
Taken down in shorthand by Mrs Kessler's clerk, and typed the same evening.
:::

**G. KESSLER:** Mr Platt, a voice on your own tape says that my robots will never leave. Where were you that night?

**R. PLATT:** Mrs Kessler, you wound me! On the night of 20 December I went to bed at the Swan Hotel at midnight and slept until eight. Ask the night porter: he wrote me in at five to midnight. Like a good boy.

**G. KESSLER:** And the tower? The voice came from the speaking tube.

**R. PLATT:** The tower! Look at me. I have never set foot in the clock room, because my bad knee will not take sixty-four steps. Ghosts can climb. Producers cannot.

**G. KESSLER:** You are not wearing your gold pin today.

**R. PLATT:** Don't remind me. I lost my lucky tie pin somewhere in town on the 21st. Twenty years I wore it. Perhaps your ghost has it, eh?

**G. KESSLER:** This is not a joke for me.

**R. PLATT:** Nor for me, dear lady. Tomorrow at three the whole country watches your factory. Smile for the camera, and your robots will sell themselves.

_End of statement._
